title: Short Stuff: Jeddah Tower
summary: Short Stuff episode on the Jeddah Tower (spelled "Jetta Tower" in the transcript's casual pronunciation), a planned kilometer-high skyscraper in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, designed by Adrian Smith. The hosts cover its origins as part of the Jeddah Economic City plan, its goal of surpassing the Burj Khalifa, the Y-shaped design chosen for wind resistance, the observation deck, mixed-use plans, construction history from the 2013 groundbreaking, the 2017 political purge and COVID-related halt, the foundation sensors, and the restart in 2023. They also mention Jeddah's association with the tomb of Eve and the Saudi crown prince's ties to the Jamal Khashoggi murder.

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the Short Stuff episode on the Jeddah Tower.

segments.title: Origins and height goal
segments.summary: The tower is described as intended to be the world's tallest building, built under Prince Alwaleed bin Talal's Jeddah Economic City plan to compete with Dubai and surpass the Burj Khalifa. It would be the first kilometer-high building, and construction went up to 2018 before halting.

segments.title: Design by Adrian Smith
segments.summary: Adrian Smith designed both the Burj Khalifa and the Jeddah Tower. The Y-shaped, tapering triangular design was chosen for wind safety, tested in a wind tunnel, and inspired by palm leaves. The hosts mention a New Yorker article on the Citicorp building's wind issues.

segments.title: Tangent on Citicorp building retrofit
segments.summary: The hosts recommend a 1995 New Yorker article, The Fifty Nine Story Crisis, about the Citicorp building and the engineering fix needed for hurricane loads.

segments.title: Observation deck and Jeddah town
segments.summary: The planned open-air observation tower sits about 287 meters up, with a helipad plan that architects reportedly rejected. The hosts also note the existing city of Jeddah on the Red Sea, which is said to hold the tomb of Eve.

segments.title: Building specs and mixed-use plan
segments.summary: Original plans call for about 80,000 tons of steel, 59 high-speed elevators, escalators and double-decker elevators. The bottom third would be offices, then a luxury hotel, with apartments in the upper floors.

segments.title: Kingdom Tower name and foundation
segments.summary: The building was originally called Kingdom Tower, with groundbreaking in April 2013. Foundation work took over a year, using very deep concrete pilings. Underground sensors in the pilings reportedly showed the foundation was sound.

segments.title: Construction halt, restart, and progress
segments.summary: Construction stopped in 2017 amid a Saudi political crisis and anti-corruption purge that arrested eleven princes, and was further delayed by COVID. Work restarted in September 2023, with 60 floors built by 2025 and the 80th floor passed in January. Mohammed bin Salman's purge and Khashoggi's murder are also raised.

segments.title: Closing and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts wrap up, noting the tower's uncertain completion timeline, and close with the iHeartRadio production credit.
